transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm a construction manager, and I'm here because... man, it's getting bad. Every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or one of the upper platforms now, my head just tells me I’m about to go over. Like I'm just going to fall. And I can see the rails are in place, you know? I know the setup is supposed to be completely safe. 

We actually just started using these new heavy-duty aluminum rail systems from a supplier out in Ohio. Supposed to be top-of-the-line stuff, really lightweight but strong. My brother-in-law actually lives in Ohio, right outside Columbus. He’s been trying to get me to come out there for a Buckeyes game for like three years now, but the flights are always just ridiculous, especially in the fall. Plus, dealing with the airport parking is a whole other headache. They just raised the daily rate at our local airport by five bucks. Can you believe that? Just to leave your truck sitting on a piece of concrete. 

But, uh... yeah, so anyway, I just can't get near the edge of a roof or a scaffold anymore without my brain telling me I'm going over.
Is this fear limited to being on scaffolds, roofs, or high places at work, or do you also experience similar feelings in other situations, like driving over bridges or standing on a balcony?

Well, bridges... I mean, I don't really know if I feel it there. Speaking of bridges, though, they're doing that massive structural overhaul on the interstate bridge right by my house. The traffic is an absolute nightmare right now. I sat there for an hour and a half last Tuesday just trying to get to the lumber yard. And my truck's AC is acting up on top of it, which makes sitting in traffic miserable. It's a 2018 F-150, usually runs like a dream, but the compressor is making this horrible rattling sound. 

My mechanic, Dave, says it's going to cost a fortune to replace. Dave's a great guy, though. We actually got our associate's degrees together back in the day. He's the one who introduced me to my wife, actually, at this backyard barbecue he threw for the Fourth of July... man, that had to be fifteen years ago now. He makes these incredible smoked ribs. 

But, uh, I'm sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, balconies and driving and stuff. Honestly, I haven't really noticed it anywhere else. I haven't been on a balcony in years, and when I'm driving over a bridge I'm usually just so annoyed about the traffic or listening to my engine rattle that I don't even look down. So I really couldn't tell you for sure if it happens there too. It's really just the job sites where it hits me.

latest_inference.note: The patient's fear appears to be limited to specific work-related situations involving heights (scaffolds, roofs, platforms), with no clear evidence of anxiety in other contexts or significant impairment outside of these specific situations. This supports a diagnosis of specific phobia, situational type. Adjustment disorder and unspecified anxiety disorder are less likely given the specific and consistent trigger.
